summary: Tested /api/notifications/* and welcome trigger on /api/auth/register against the preview backend. 10/10 pytest cases pass. The admin-auth fix on /broadcast (role check → ADMIN_EMAIL match) works correctly: admin (soportefactuya@gmail.com) gets 200 with {ok:true, sent:N}, non-admin gets 403 'Admin only', and broadcast notifications are persisted per user and visible via GET /api/notifications/. Welcome notification with type='welcome' and link='/subscription?coupon=LANZAMIENTO50' is created on register.

minor.issue: Silently returns {ok:true} even when the notification id does not exist or belongs to another user (matched_count==0 ignored intentionally per code comment). Not a bug per current spec but worth confirming product intent — could be misleading to API consumers.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/notifications.py defines its own AsyncIOMotorClient via os.environ['MONGO_URL'] but does not call load_dotenv. This works only because server.py loads dotenv first; if this module is ever imported standalone it would KeyError. Consider centralising the db handle in a shared module.

Both routes/auth.py and routes/admin.py hard-code ADMIN_EMAIL = 'soportefactuya@gmail.com' (now also in notifications.py). DRY violation — extract to a single config constant (e.g. utils/admin.py or env var ADMIN_EMAIL) to avoid future drift.

routes/auth.py imports `from routes.notifications import create_notification` inside the register handler (lazy). Fine for avoiding circular imports but slightly inefficient on every register call — could be a module-level import.

routes/notifications.py uses `user=Depends(get_current_user)` where get_current_user is the same callable bound to GET /auth/me via @router.get decorator. FastAPI does not double-register because the decorator returns the original function, but reusing a route function as a dependency couples the two semantics. Consider extracting a pure get_current_user dependency separate from the /me endpoint.

Welcome trigger is wrapped in try/except that only logs at WARNING — silent failure: if create_notification crashes the user still gets registered with no notification and no visible error. Acceptable for UX, but ensure logs are monitored.
seed_data_creation: Each test that needed an unread notification created a fresh broadcast titled TEST_* with a uuid suffix. The register test creates a TEST_welcome_*@example.com user and deletes it via DELETE /api/auth/account at the end (best-effort cleanup).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Notifications endpoints verified end-to-end on preview. Re-run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_notifications.py -v. Tests are idempotent and self-cleaning. If running repeatedly note that each run will add several TEST_ broadcast notifications to every user's inbox; safe but accumulative.
rca of the issue: Original 403 in production: /api/notifications/broadcast checked `user.role == 'admin'`, but UserResponse pydantic model does not expose a `role` field (and the project's admin pattern is email match, see routes/admin.py:verify_admin). Fix applied in notifications.py L160-169 now fetches the current user document from db.users by id and compares its email to ADMIN_EMAIL='soportefactuya@gmail.com' (case-insensitive), matching the established pattern. Verified: admin login → broadcast returns 200; non-admin → 403.
